title: Create canonical driver/CUDA matrix and isolated runner sandboxes for reliable load harnesses
creator: Ava Patel
description:
Problem: Our tokens/sec and p95 regression alerts have noisy signals caused by subtle differences in OS drivers, CUDA builds, and non-deterministic runner images. Several past regressions were traced to mismatched driver stacks or ephemeral runner changes. We need a canonical, reproducible baseline for load harnesses so benchmarks are comparable across time and CI runs.

Goal: Define a minimal, pinned driver/CUDA/image matrix and provision isolated 'runner sandboxes' that mirror production serving stacks. These sandboxes will be used by the benchmark harness and CI validators (pre-merge smoke and nightly regression pipelines). This ticket covers discovery, image naming convention, sandbox orchestration, CI gating, and rollout plan.

Scope / Deliverables:
- Canonical driver/CUDA matrix document (supported driver versions, CUDA minor versions, and corresponding pinned base image tags).
- Build pipeline for pinned runner images (immutable tags like rwd-bench:cuda12.1-driver535-20250901). Images must include kernel module version metadata and preinstalled diagnostics.
- Sandbox orchestration: lightweight k8s namespaces with node selectors to target GPU types (A100/GPUv2, H100, etc.) and taints to isolate from prod. Each sandbox exposes a stable IP and /health/bench endpoint for harness discovery.
- CI validators: a bench-smoke job that executes a canonical tokens/sec and p95 check for each image; nightly regression pipeline that compares time-series to golden baselines and opens ENG tickets on regression thresholds.
- Acceptance criteria and success metrics: reproducibility within ±3% tokens/sec for synthetic baseline; p95 variance <5% across 5 consecutive runs; CI runs that fail due to infra mismatch must be categorized separately from model regressions.

Design decisions & trade-offs:
- Immutable image tags vs floating tags: choose immutability for reproducibility; we will create 1 stable tag per matrix entry and a lightweight 'latest-canonical' pointer tag for convenience.
- Storage and retention: keeping pinned images increases storage costs. We'll retain the last 6 canonical tags per CUDA-driver pair and provide a reclamation job.
- Sandboxes vs full prod clones: sandboxes will intentionally be smaller (single-node pools) to reduce cost but will match driver/kernel stack and runtime libraries exactly. This avoids flakiness while reducing spend.

Implementation notes:
- Image build: use existing image-builder pipeline (kaniko) to create minimal runner images. Embed a /metadata file with driver, cuda, kernel, git-commit, and build-timestamp.
- Tag format: rwd-bench:<model>-cuda<CUDAMajor>.<CUDAMinor>-drv<DriverMajor>-<YYYYMMDD>-<gitshort>. Example: rwd-bench:gpt-small-cuda12.1-drv535-20250901-a1b2c3d
- Benchmark harness changes: add --sandbox-tag and --env-matrix flags to the harness to pin the image and driver matrix used. Harness should collect tokens/sec, p95, tail-percentiles and include the image/driver metadata in the artifact.
- CI: add bench-smoke to pre-merge that runs a short 5k-token run on a synthetic prompt; nightly-regression compares signal against baseline using Kendall tau and percentage drift rules.

Dependencies and related work: this ticket coordinates with ENG-62458 (stable-benchmark-fabric-driver-image-contract) and ENG-34321 (runtime-contracts-and-ci-validators-for-load-harness-repro). We'll also reference console dashboards for p95 tracking and regression alerts.

Risks and mitigations:
- Risk: Hardware variance (different OEM driver builds) causes unavoidable noise. Mitigation: label sandboxes with driver build SHAs and restrict benchmark comparisons to identical driver builds unless explicit drift tests are run.
- Risk: Image drift if rebuilds are not strictly pinned. Mitigation: adopt single-source-of-truth manifests stored in S3 + signed metadata.

Next steps:
1) Finalize matrix doc and tag naming (this ticket).
2) Prototype image build and publish one canonical tag per CUDA 12.1/11.8 + driver pair.
3) Stand up sandbox k8s namespace and wire harness discovery.
4) Add bench-smoke to PR CI and run nightly regression job.

Acceptance tests (manual):
- Run harness against rwd-bench:gpt-small-cuda12.1-drv535-<tag>; verify collected artifact includes /metadata and tokens/sec within expected baseline.
- Trigger nightly-regression and confirm no false positives on control runs.

Links and artifacts:
- Design doc (Confluence): https://redwood.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/ENG/pages/Bench+Driver+Matrix
- Prototype PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runner-images/pull/412
- Regression dashboard: https://console.redwood.ai/dashboards/bench-regressions
